UnitStatement: An agent is operationally defined as an LLM plus instructions plus file access plus tool use.
The agent definition specifies an operational runtime system rather than a metaphysical category.
The agent definition does not make an AI agent a responsible person or bearer of professional duty.
Agent 1 orchestrates instructions for Agent 2.
Good agents specialize in one type of thing and only that one type.
Good agents are orchestrated in workflows between decision points.
Orchestrating agents between decision points supports speed and trustworthy output in professional engineering work.
A great agent is modeled as Agent 0 wrapping Agent 1 wrapping Agent 2.
Agent 0 brings the human and Agent 1 into alignment.
The model presents three layers of nested agents as sufficient.
More complex agent architectures can exist but have tradeoffs.
Agent 0 is the Architect.
The Architect writes and maintains instructions after the human determines alignment.
Agent 1 is the Manager.
The Manager orchestrates which instructions and files and tools go to which specialist.
Agent 2 is the Specialist.
The Specialist takes actions according to instructions.
In Chirality an AI agent is a bounded artificial actor.
A Chirality AI agent can read files and use tools.
A Chirality AI agent can generate claims and modify project state within its write scope.
In regulated practice an AI agent is treated as an other whose work a human professional supervises and reviews before reliance.
A system-question classifies the runtime as an agent in the technical sense.
A treatment-question classifies agent work as delegated work under human supervision and review and accountability.
The human remains the accountable party.
The agent contributes content and action inside a governed workflow.
The human decides what to rely on.
Narrowing the scope of Agent 2 reduces the probability of hallucination.
A scoped Agent 2 only needs to execute the specific function Agent 1 handed it.
Agents propose and humans decide.
No agent can approve deliverables.
No agent can resolve conflicts.
No agent can issue work for reliance.
The human stays in responsible charge throughout the workflow.
The agent system accelerates work rather than decisions.
Smaller contexts and specialized instructions process faster and cheaper than massive general-purpose prompts.
Bad output indicates Agent 2 tools should be fixed.
A wrong task attempt indicates Agent 1 instructions should be fixed.
A misunderstood goal indicates Agent 0 alignment should be fixed.
A team of agents is a project-management structure in Chirality.
Chirality treats decomposition as an organizational device for structuring work.
Chirality treats folder hierarchy as an organizational device for structuring work.
Chirality treats stable IDs as an organizational device for structuring work.
Chirality treats lifecycle states as an organizational device for structuring work.
Chirality treats dependencies as an organizational device for structuring work.
Chirality treats gates as an organizational device for structuring work.
Chirality treats reviews as an organizational device for structuring work.
Chirality treats change controls as an organizational device for structuring work.
Chirality makes work structure directly inspectable in the filesystem.
Many-agent orchestration matters for legibility and not only parallelism.
Delegated work must be legible enough for human supervision and review and responsibility acceptance.
The human interfaces with a single Agent 1 instance through chat.
Agent 1 assigns tasks to nested Agent 2 instances running in parallel.
In fan-out Agent 1 receives direction from the human and assigns tasks to Agent 2 instances.
In process Agent 2 instances execute simultaneously.
In fan-in Agent 1 collects results and returns the final output to the human.
Failure in one Agent 2 instance leaves the other Agent 2 instances unaffected.
Each Agent 2 instance spawns with zero state.
Zero-state spawning prevents context drift from previous tasks.
In the invoice example each Agent 2 instance extracts Date from a single PDF.
In the invoice example each Agent 2 instance extracts Amount from a single PDF.
In the invoice example each Agent 2 instance extracts Vendor from a single PDF.
In the invoice example Agent 1 collects results and merges them into a CSV.
Invoice processing is done by Agent 2 types orchestrated by Agent 1.
Great agents are composed of good agents.
Chirality implements the agent model with a governed agent instruction suite.
Chirality implements the agent model with a formal invariant system.
Chirality implements the agent model with governance documents that make the system auditable.
